evidence: Time-varying public demands: live updates within 15 s without reload (instruction.md:5; hireops_rules.md:117-123), preservation of typed text/focus/open card/open conversation/scroll during updates (rules:121-123), scrolled-up arrival notice (rules:156-160), earlier-page load keeping place (rules:144-147), live seen marks and unread counts (rules:117-119,149-166), put-back with focus on refusal (rules:82-85), session end mid-draft (rules:168-175). Theme and phone layout are explicitly not required (instruction.md:11), and visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required', so no resize/toggle leg is owed. Every time-varying demand is exercised with actions and waits rather than a still paint: functional/prompt.md:47 (V) 'Without reloading or clicking in this page, wait up to 15 seconds (a wait-for call, or snapshots; accept what is present at the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds)' graded by hro_live_board (functional/judge.toml:285-291); prompt.md:41 (U) 'wait up to 15 seconds after the other person acts' for unread/seen (hro_unread_counts 329-336, hro_seen 347-354) and the scrolled-up arrival in Noor's long thread (hro_unread_scrolled_up 338-345); T watches the reply 'arrive on Rafael's open conversation without reload' (hro_msg_exchange 293-300); L checks the refused full-Interview move puts the card back with focus via document.activeElement (hro_refused_put_back 131-138). Polish dimension is dedicated to in-flight behaviour: polish/prompt.md:14 'After that action do not reload, navigate, click or type in the observed page until the update has been seen or 15 seconds have passed. Read document.activeElement, field values and scroll offsets with page.evaluate'; polish/judge.toml:23 types an unsaved note in an open card, scrolls, has another recruiter move a card, then checks details open, note text, activeElement, scroll not reset and 'typing more appends to it' (catches caret reset); :32 same for a half-typed reply during message arrival; :41 measures getBoundingClientRect().top of the top message before/after loading earlier; :50 aborts one send; :59 ends the session in a second tab then presses Enter. Adversarial: a full re-render-on-poll app (closes card, wipes note, resets caret/scroll) fails hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread; a reload-only app fails hro_live_board/hro_msg_exchange/hro_seen/hro_unread_counts; an app jumping to bottom on arrival fails hro_unread_scrolled_up; an app jumping on 'load earlier' fails hro_pol_earlier_place. Conforming alternatives are tolerated: page vs container scroll, no scroll at this viewport ('record that no scroll exists and judge the other legs'), polling/SSE/sockets, 15 s first-snapshot tolerance, UI-side pre-refusal accepted for put-back. Golden scripted observations (hash-verified, not a judge run) show the golden satisfies these legs: workspace.json 'live board ... open card, note draft and focus kept' arrival_ms 805; 'arrival while reading keeps draft, focus and scroll and is not marked read until viewed'; 'seen receipt and unread badges update live'.
notes: Note (no defect): rules:84 'A move appears on the mover's board immediately' (optimistic display) is not separately timed; a sub-second timing distinction is discouraged by REVIEW_POLICY 'Tool feasibility', and the observable put-back is graded.

Note (low): hro_pol_live_board requires the other card's move to be 'visible on this page' while a card's details are open; an app whose detail view fully replaces the board could get 0. instruction.md:5 ('show up on my board ... without closing the card I have open') implies board and open card coexist, so this is consistent with the public brief; a modal overlay still leaves the board in the DOM snapshot.
Note: the live unread total is read only with Rafael on the Conversations view; live total on other views is not separately exercised (not a stated separate requirement).

Note: the golden script's live-board group (workspace.cjs:352-369) asserts note/focus/detail preservation but not scroll; the judge prompt covers scroll, and golden scroll behaviour is unmeasured by any judge run.
